# dsh-prompt-history
English | 中文
Terminal-style input for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI composer: Claude Code-style prompt history, se
lection copy/quote, and right-click paste.
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI input composer enhancement plugin. Accurately recreates Claude Code's
arrow-key prompt history recall and double-Escape workflows, provides selection toolbar quotation/a
uto-copy, right-click Linux-style direct paste, and unblocks inline slash completion under claimed c
ommand states. Pure client-side UI behavior with zero third-party dependencies, issuing zero model r
tates. Pure client-side UI behavior with zero third-party dependencies, issuing zero model requests.

## What It Is
A keyboard-first ergonomics suite tailored for the DSH browser composer.
During routine LLM-assisted development, manually retyping previous prompts, navigating across multi
-line drafts, and repeatedly switching to the mouse for selection copying break the developer's trai
n of thought. `@wenaixi/dsh-prompt-history` bridges mature terminal command-line muscle memory and C
laude Code interaction patterns directly into the DSH browser workspace.

Client-side architectural boundaries:
- **Zero session event pollution**: emits no synthetic session

events and leaves the agent execution loop intact;
- **Zero model requests**: pure UI behavior cons

uming zero model tokens;
- **Zero external network endpoints**: hosts no HTTP services; all configur

ations strictly adhere to the host `ConfigForm` contract;
- **Safe execution boundary**: recalled an
d quoted text only populates the local composer draft; content is never dispatched to the model unti
l the user presses Enter.
## Core Features

### 1. Claude Code-Style Arrow-Key & Emacs History Recall
- **Backward traversal on the first visual
row (↑ or Ctrl+P)**: when the caret rests on the first visual row of the composer, pressing ↑ or `C
trl+P` walks backward through historical prompts starting from the newest entry. The caret parks at

the beginning of each recalled line; reaching the oldest entry stops without wrapping.
- **Forward t
raversal on the last visual row (↓ or Ctrl+N)**: while in history browsing mode with the caret on th
e last visual row, pressing ↓ or `Ctrl+N` moves toward newer prompts, parking the caret at the line
end. Traversing past the newest entry faithfully restores the original draft typed prior to browsing

(restoring an empty line if started empty).
- **Edit exits browsing**: typing any character while b

rowsing history immediately exits browsing mode, retaining the current draft.
- **Visual row wrappin
g & multi-line geometric detection**: utilizes actual screen geometry (`getBoundingClientRect`). Whe
ther a draft wraps across multiple visual rows due to width limits (Visual Row Wrapping) or contains
true linebreaks, arrow keys first traverse across visual rows; history recall is gated strictly at

the top or bottom edges, eliminating accidental history jumps while editing multi-line text.
- **Con
secutive duplicate deduplication**: strictly conforms to Claude Code specification; submitting ident
ical prompts consecutively collapses duplicates into a single entry, preventing consecutive identica

l recalls.
- **IME composition guard**: host `[data-composer-composing]` attribute and native `isCom
posing` guards ensure that arrow keys never trigger history recall while converting IME candidates.

### 2. Reverse Interactive History Search (Ctrl+R & Double-Escape)
- **Ctrl+R shortcut**: matches of
ficial Claude Code terminal behavior; pressing `Ctrl+R` inside the composer immediately summons the

reverse search overlay. Pressing `Ctrl+R` again while searching cycles to older matches.
- **Double-
Escape trigger**: with an empty composer draft, pressing Escape twice within 800 ms also brings up t

he prompt-history overlay.
- **Real-time filtering & highlighting**: keyboard focus remains on the c
omposer. Typing performs live substring and character subsequence fuzzy matching (`fuzzyMatch`, e.g.

, typing `dpl` matches `deploy now`), visually highlighting matched characters in the list.
- **Dire
ct keyboard control**: ↑ and ↓ navigate the active highlight (clamped at boundaries without wrapping
, never modifying the underlying draft), Home and End jump to edges, Enter or Tab populates the high

lighted item, and Escape closes the overlay, restoring the prior draft.
- **Relative timestamps & wi
de-screen preview**: each row displays a relative age indicator (`5m / 3h / 2d`). On viewports ≥ 100
0px wide, a right-hand pane provides an expanded multi-line preview of the highlighted item. The foo
ter live-counts "matches / total".

### 3. Double-Escape Smart Draft Clearing
- With a non-empty composer draft, the first Escape displa

ys a subtle hint ("Press Esc again to clear input") while passing the event through;
- Pressing Esca
pe a second time within 800 ms saves the current draft into history and clears the composer (the cle

ared content remains recallable via ↑);
- Double-Escape can be toggled in settings; when disabled, E
scape is handed entirely back to the host.

### 4. Universal Input Formats & Lossless Long-Session Recall
- **Universal input format coverage**:
seamlessly supports standard prompts as well as slash commands (faithfully reconstructing full `/cm

d args` prototypes), interactive question replies, and dynamic command inputs.
